findings.title: E4 control sd impossible
findings.description: The self-evaluation measure is a single seven-point integer item, so the observations must be whole numbers. With a mean of exactly 4.20, at least a fifth of responses must depart from 4, which forces a sample SD of roughly 0.41 or more; 0.21 is below the floor. Verified independently by R's rsprite2 (infeasible=true), and robust to the unknown control-group size: no integer sample exists at n = 15, 20, 30 or 60. n=15 is the value implied by the reported degrees of freedom. Value confirmed identically in both the XML and the PDF version of record.

findings.title: E3 target attractiveness out of range (Experiment 3, Manipulation check)
findings.description: Experiment 3 states its attractiveness ratings used 'the seam [same] measures used in Experiments 1 and 2', both of which explicitly define a seven-point scale (1 = not at all attractive, 7 = extremely attractive). A mean of 7.33 exceeds that maximum and is unattainable at any n. The bound is stated by the paper via explicit cross-reference rather than assumed by me. Either the mean is wrong or the methods description of the scale is wrong; a nine-point scale would reconcile 7.33 and 4.17 around a midpoint of 5, but the paper does not say that. Note also that the same value 7.33 is reported in the same paragraph as the positive-mood mean, and both attractiveness SDs are identically 1.19.

findings.title: E4 sample size discrepancy
findings.description: This is the one study of five whose sample arithmetic does not reconcile. The pilot (42+3=45), Experiment 1 (43+4=47), Experiment 2 (126+15=141) and Experiment 3 (8 cells of 12 = 96) all reconcile exactly against their stated Ns, which is what makes Experiment 4's 60-participant shortfall stand out rather than looking like a routine reporting convention.

findings.title: Statcheck body (Whole body text (Pilot, Experiments 1-4))

findings.notes: Downgraded from the tool's highly_suspicious to indeterminate, deliberately. The tool recomputes a ONE-WAY ANOVA, but the paper's F carries df_error=118, i.e. it comes from the residual of the full 2x2x2 model. The one-way error term uses df=124; moving six further effects (all reported as Fs<1) out of the residual raises the mean square and lowers F by roughly the ratio 124/118, which brings the expected value to about 725 -- close to the printed 716.92. The apparent discrepancy is therefore largely explained by the model I could fit versus the model they fitted, and I am not treating it as evidence against the paper. The same caveat does not apply to the pilot ANOVA, which really is one-way.

findings.title: Multiplicity e4 anova
findings.description: The paper applies no multiplicity correction anywhere, but for this family it does not matter: the p-values are mostly far below alpha, and only the marginal mood-by-direction effect (p=.04) fails Bonferroni. Recorded because the absence of correction is a real feature of the paper's analysis and because the result is a null one worth stating rather than leaving implicit. The authors do report supplementary Tukey HSD tests in footnotes 2 and 5, which is more than most papers of this era did.

findings.title: E1 simple effect df inconsistent (Experiment 1, Self-evaluations)
findings.description: Every other test in Experiment 1 uses df_error=43, correct for N=47 in a 2x2 design. This one simple effect uses 46, which is N-1 and corresponds to no error term in the stated design. findings.title: Identical sds weak signal (Experiment 3 Manipulation check; Table 2 Similarity row)
findings.description: Three coincidences of repeated values, each individually unremarkable: two attractiveness SDs identical at 1.19 in the same sentence; two similarity means identical at 6.81 in adjacent Table 2 cells; two pilot self-evaluation means identical at 6.98. Rulebook rule 8 -- individually weak signals, reported but not escalated. They are noted because they co-occur with the impossibility findings, and because the SD pair 1.19/1.19 sits in the same sentence as the out-of-range mean 7.33. Recorded as indeterminate: repeated values are ordinary in small samples and prove nothing on their own.
